description: Landing on the Moon is not about finding the brightest spot. It is about choosing the right place at the right time: a site that sees the Sun, sees the Earth, and keeps the link alive for the whole mission. The same crater, with the same sunlight, can be a safe bet on one start date and a 127-hour blackout on another. We turn real NASA data into one clear answer for any point near the lunar south pole: where, and when.
summary: LUNARIS is a tool for choosing a lunar landing site by place and by date. For any point near the lunar south pole it answers three questions: does the spot see the Sun, does it see the Earth, and could it keep a communication link alive for the whole mission? It combines real NASA data (LOLA elevation models, SPICE ephemerides, Deep Space Network station geometry) and returns solar capacity, link continuity and a suitability verdict per mission window, with maps and a 3D viewer of the site. Its key insight is timing: the same spot with the same sunlight scores APTO 97.4 on one start date and CONDICIONAL 73.9 on another, because of a 127-hour communications blackout. At Mons Malapert, which scores 98.4, only 5 of 353 start dates pass every check. LUNARIS tells planners where and when. It labels top spots as candidates, not certified sites, and states its limits on screen.
details:
WHAT IT DOES. For any point near the lunar south pole and any mission start date, LUNARIS computes solar capacity (sunlight, longest night, panel power), Earth visibility and communication continuity through NASA Deep Space Network stations, and a suitability score with APTO / CONDICIONAL / NO APTO verdicts from eight gates (G0-G7). Earth visibility is treated as continuity of the link (longest gap without contact), not a single yes/no. It proposes the best start dates, ranks candidate sites, and shows everything on a navigable south-pole map and a 3D viewer (real LROC photo, true Sun and Earth positions, observer's-eye view).

WHY IT MATTERS. A bright spot is not a landing site. At Shackleton the same spot with 100% sunlight is APTO (97.4) if the mission starts on 12 Dec 2026 and CONDICIONAL (73.9) on 6 Dec, because of a 127-hour blackout. Planners need to know when a site works, not only where.

HOW IT WAS BUILT. Python 3.11, Streamlit, NumPy/SciPy, rasterio, SPICE (SpiceyPy), three.js. Data: LOLA DEMs (5 m and 80 m), SPICE kernels, DSN station geometry, LROC imagery, Diviner maps, checked against JPL Horizons. 997 automated tests.

HONESTY. Top-ranked spots are labelled candidates, not certified sites: they do not match the published illumination map to within +/-0.2-0.3. Bad results are published on purpose and the error of the coarse far-field mode is stated on screen. The interface is currently in Spanish.

OPEN SOURCE. Apache-2.0. Method, validation and limits are documented in the repository.
